newsitem.title: FRANCE: French film director Marcel Carne dies.
newsitem.headline: French film director Marcel Carne dies.

text.p: French film director Marcel Carne, who fathered a cinematic legend with "Les Enfants du Paradis" in the 1940s, died on Thursday, a spokeswoman for the culture ministry said. He was 90.
Carne, a poineer the French "Film noir", died in hospital in Clamart near Paris.

Carne won widespread acclaim for classics "Quai des Brumes" and "Hotel du Nord" in the 1930s and 1940s. He will probably best be remembered for "Les Enfants du Paradis", which evoked the sleazy street life of Paris in the mid-19th century.
He worked consistently for three decades after World War Two but his career was plagued by critical and commercial setbacks and he never recovered the success of his golden years.
Despite his age, Carne had proved his stamina at the 1992 Cannes film festival, partying until the early hours every night.
Born in Paris in 1906, Carne chose not to take up his father's trade as a carpenter. He quickly found a path into the emerging art of filmmaking.

Obsessed by the cinema early on, he took lessons in photography and became editor of Film-Hebdo magazine. He was later hired as an assistant to director Rene Clair and made his first full-length production, "Jenny", in 1936.
